name: Progress & incompleteness

evidence.basis: Goal-gradient: effort accelerates near a goal (Hull 1932; field-validated by Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng 2006). Endowed-progress effect (Nunes & Dreze 2006). Zeigarnik effect (unfinished tasks stay cognitively active) — real but with mixed replication.
evidence.effect_size_note: Goal-gradient acceleration is well supported in field data; the endowed-progress effect (giving artificial head-start) is robust; the classic Zeigarnik memory effect is smaller and less reliably replicated than its popular reputation.

mechanism_summary_for_context: People are pulled to close what is unfinished, and they push harder the closer the goal appears. A visible progress indicator toward an attainable goal increases completion; an unfinished state creates low-grade tension that motivates return. Two levers: show progress (bars, steps, checklists) and give a sense of head-start (progress already made). Distinct from loss aversion — this is the pull of completion, not the fear of loss.

preconditions.reason: requires a goal decomposable into visible steps or progress; not applicable to single-action flows

applicability.culture_note: Goal pursuit is broadly universal; preferred granularity and visual style of progress are L3 surface parameters

implementations.generation_directive: Show a visible progress indicator toward a concrete, attainable goal (steps completed, profile completeness, setup checklist). The goal must be real and reachable; the progress shown must be true. Break large goals into visible sub-steps so acceleration near each sub-goal compounds.

Grant a genuine head-start toward the first goal (pre-complete a real first step the user has effectively already taken, e.g. 'account created ✓'). The head-start must correspond to something real; inventing fake progress the user didn't make is forbidden.

Surface a genuinely unfinished item the user cares about (draft, incomplete profile, unstarted-but-set-up task) as a gentle open loop that invites completion. Not manufactured incompleteness; only real unfinished states the user would want closed.

hard_rules.rule: Displayed progress must reflect real state; fabricated or inflated progress bars are forbidden
Endowed progress must correspond to something the user actually did or received; inventing fake completed steps is forbidden
The goal must be genuinely reachable; do not create endless or moving goalposts that never complete
Do not artificially fragment or leave things incomplete solely to create tension; open loops must be real, user-relevant unfinished states

constraints.boundary_test: Is the progress and the goal real and reachable — or is completion engineered to always recede?

relations.note: Near-complete progress can be framed as loss-if-abandoned (hybrid with LA-01), but the core driver here is the pull of completion, not fear of loss
Progress toward goals supports habit formation; distinct — HA-04 is the recurring loop, ZE-07 is goal-directed progress

reference_examples.what: 'Profile 80% complete' meter — canonical progress indicator driving completion of a multi-step goal
Endowed-progress effect: cards pre-stamped with 'bonus' stamps complete faster than empty cards toward the same required count (Nunes & Dreze)
Visible unit progress and next-lesson framing use goal-gradient acceleration toward attainable checkpoints
